Warmly devoted; hearty; sincere; earnest.

ex.ja: トムの母親は敬虔なカトリック教徒だった。

en: Having a quality that divides or separates.

ex.en: The new law is a divisive issue.
ex.ja: 新しい法律は意見が分かれる問題だ。

note.ja: divide（分ける）+ -sive。「分裂を招く」。

en: A hard, dense, deep black wood from various subtropical and tropical trees, especially of the genus Diospyros.
A tree that yields such wood.
Made of ebony wood.
A deep, dark black colour.

ex.en: The piano keys were made of ebony.
ex.ja: ピアノの鍵盤は黒檀で作られていた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 ebenos から。エジプト語に由来する。「黒檀」。

en: experienced, mediated via the physical body (typically in contrast to mental experience)

ex.en: These ideas are embodied in the constitution.
ex.ja: これらの理念は憲法に具体化されている。

note.ja: embody（具現化する）+ -ed。em + body（体）。「体を与える」→「具現化された」。

en: In the reproductive cycle, the stage after the fertilization of the egg that precedes the development into a fetus.
An organism in the earlier stages of development before it emerges from the egg, or before metamorphosis.

embryo.ety: Borrowed from Medieval Latin embryō, from Ancient Greek ἔμβρυον (émbruon, “fetus”), from ἐν (en, “in-”) + βρύω (brúō, “to grow, swell”).

ex.en: The plan is still in its embryo stage.
ex.ja: その計画はまだ初期段階にある。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 embryon ＝ en（中に）+ bryein（膨らむ）。「中で膨らむもの」→「胚・胎児」。

en: To occur afterwards, as a result or effect.

ensue.ety: From Old French ensu-, stem of some conjugated forms of ensuivre (“follow close upon, come afterward”) (French ensuivre), from Latin īnsequere, from īnsequi (“to pursue, follow, follow after; come next”), from in- (“upon”) (see in-) + sequi (“follow”) (see sequel).

ex.en: Much confusion ensued following this news report.
ex.ja: そのニュースで非常に混乱した。

ex.en: The train was derailed, and panic ensued.
ex.ja: 列車が脱線すると、たちまちパニック状態になった。

note.ja: en（〜に）+ su（続く）+ e。ラテン語 sequi（続く）から。後に続く →「続いて起こる」。

en: Unsteady, random; prone to unexpected changes; not consistent.
Deviating from normal opinions or actions; eccentric; odd.
A rock moved from one location to another, usually by a glacier.
Anything that has erratic characteristics.

en: A long, pointed canine tooth used for biting and tearing flesh.
A long, pointed tooth in snakes, used for injecting venom.
To enable to catch or tear; to furnish with fangs.

fang.ety: From clipping of fangtooth, from Middle English *fangtooth, *fengtooth, from Old English fengtōþ (“molar tooth”), from feng, preterite of fōn (“to catch, take, seize”). Cognate with German Fangzahn (“fang”, literally “catch-tooth”) and Dutch vangtand. See also related senses of Etymology 3 below.

ex.en: The snake showed its fangs.
ex.ja: ヘビは牙をむいた。

note.ja: 古英語 fang（捕らえたもの）から。「捕らえるもの」→「牙」。

en: A religious festival.
A festive occasion.
To take part in a festive celebration; to party.

fiesta.ety: Borrowed from Spanish fiesta, from Late Latin festa, from the plural of festum (“feast”). Doublet of feast, fest, and fete.

ex.en: The whole town joined the summer fiesta.
ex.ja: 町中の人が夏の祭りに参加した。

note.ja: スペイン語 fiesta（祭り）から。ラテン語 festa。festival、feast と同じ。

en: Foolishness that results from a lack of foresight or lack of practicality.
Thoughtless action resulting in tragic consequence.

folly.ety: Inherited from Middle English folie, from Old French folie (“madness”), from the adjective fol (“mad, insane”).

ex.en: There's always a good part in human folly.
ex.ja: 人間の愚かさには必ず何か良い部分もあります。

ex.en: I cannot help laughing at your folly.
ex.ja: 君の愚かさには笑わずにはいられない。

ex.en: I cannot help laughing at my folly.
ex.ja: 私は自分の愚かさを笑わずにいられない。

note.ja: 古フランス語 folie（狂気）から。fol（ばか）、fool と同じ。「愚かさ」。

ja: 予見できる（in the foreseeable future：当分は）

en: Able to be foreseen or anticipated.

ex.en: Prices will keep rising in the foreseeable future.
ex.ja: 当分は物価が上がり続けるだろう。

note.ja: foresee + -able。「予見できる」→ in the foreseeable future（当面は）。

en: A man of French birth or nationality.
A home-made tool used by bricklayers to cut excess mortar from newly pointed brickwork.

Frenchman.ety: From Middle English Frenshman. By surface analysis, French + -man.

ex.en: He is not an American but a Frenchman.
ex.ja: 彼はアメリカ人ではなくフランス人です。

ex.en: I have a daughter who's married to a Frenchman.
ex.ja: フランス人と結婚した娘がいます。

ex.en: We have a daughter who is married to a Frenchman.
ex.ja: フランス人と結婚した娘がいます。

note.ja: French + man。「フランス人（男性）」。

en: A gas or vapour/vapor that is strong-smelling or dangerous to inhale.
A material that has been vaporized from the solid or liquid state to the gas state and re-coalesced to the solid state.
To expose (something) to fumes; specifically, to expose wood, etc., to ammonia in order to produce dark tints.
To apply or offer incense to.

fume.ety: From Middle English fume, from Old French fum (“smoke, steam, vapour”), from Latin fūmus (“vapour, smoke”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰuh₂mós (“smoke”), from *dʰewh₂- (“to smoke, raise dust”). Doublet of thymus and thymos. More at dun, dusk, dust.

ex.en: Don't just sit there and fume. Tell me what's wrong.
ex.ja: ムスッとして座ってないで、何がいけないのか言えよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 fumus（煙）から。「煙」→ 怒りで頭から煙が出る →「いきり立つ」。perfume と同じ。

en: Of eyes: glistening but not focusing on anything in particular; showing no liveliness.
Having a glaze (a coating).
A glazed donut, one with a coating such as sugar or chocolate.

ex.en: I bought a glazed donut.
ex.ja: 私はつやのあるグレーズドーナツを買った。

note.ja: glaze（つやを出す）+ -ed。glass と同じ語源。「つや出しした」→ 目が「どんよりした」。

en: The wood from any dicotyledonous tree, without regard to its hardness.
(in more general use) As the preceding, but limited to those that are commercial timbers, and are at least average in hardness.
Made of interlocking hardwood boards.

hardwood.ety: From hard + wood. The term refers to the seed coat of the tree's seeds; it does not refer to the degree of hardness of the tree's wood, but it seems to do so and is usually assumed to do so by speakers not well informed about trees and timber.

ex.en: I prefer hardwood floors to carpet.
ex.ja: 私はカーペットよりも硬い木の床が好きです。

note.ja: hard（かたい）+ wood（木）。「堅木・広葉樹材」。softwood（針葉樹材）の対。

en: The state of being high.
A title of respect when referring to a prince or princess.

highness.ety: From Middle English hyghnesse; equivalent to high + -ness.

ex.en: "Thank you, Your Highness," said the guard.
ex.ja: 「ありがとうございます、殿下」と衛兵は言った。

note.ja: high + -ness。「高貴さ」→ 王族の敬称。

en: Realization or understanding of the significance and nature of events after they have occurred.

hindsight.ety: From hind + sight, 19th c. Compare Latinate retrospect.

ex.en: With 20/20 hindsight, he could tell why they lost the game.
ex.ja: 今となっては後の祭りだったが、彼はどうして自分達が試合に負けたのかよくわかった。

ex.en: The general had 20/20 hindsight about the defeat, but no foresight at all.
ex.ja: 将軍は結局のところ敗北を認めたが、予想だにしなかったことである。

note.ja: hind（後ろの）+ sight（見ること）。「後から見ること」→「後知恵」。

en: A jointed or flexible device that allows the pivoting of a door etc.
A naturally occurring joint resembling such hardware in form or action, as in the shell of a bivalve.
To attach by, or equip with a hinge.
To depend on something.

hinge.ety: From Middle English henge (“hinge”), from Old English *henġ or *henġe (“hinge”), from Proto-West Germanic *hangiju or *hangī; compare Old English *henġe- in henġeclif (“overhanging cliff”), Old English henġen (“hanging; that upon which a thing is hung”). Akin to Scots heenge (“hinge”), Saterland Frisian Hänge (“hinge”), Low German henge (“hook, hinge, handle”), Dutch heng (“moving leaf of a hinge”), Dutch geheng (“hinge”), Middle Dutch henghe, hanghe (“hook, hinge, handle”), Scots hingel (“any attachment by which something is hung or fastened”), Dutch hengel (“hook”), hengsel (“handle”), diale

ex.en: He hung the gate on hinges.
ex.ja: 彼は門をちょうつがいで取り付けた。

note.ja: 中英語 henge（ぶら下がるもの）から。hang と同じ。「ちょうつがい」→「〜次第である（hinge on）」。

en: The state of being indifferent.
Unbiased impartiality.

indifference.ety: From Middle French indifférence, from Late Latin indifferentia. By surface analysis, in- + difference.

ex.en: It is a matter of indifference to him.
ex.ja: それは彼にとってたいした問題ではない。

ex.en: She assumed an air of indifference.
ex.ja: 彼女は知らん顔をした。

ex.en: These problems have arisen as a result of indifference.
ex.ja: これらの問題は無関心の結果として生じたものだ。

note.ja: in（否定）+ difference（違い）。「どちらでも違いがない」→「無関心」。

en: Absolutely necessary or requisite; that one cannot do without.
Unbendable, that cannot be set aside or ignored.
A thing that is not dispensable; a necessity.

indispensable.ety: Borrowed from Middle French indispensable, from Medieval Latin indispensābilis, corresponding to in- + dispensable.

ex.en: Both air and water are indispensable for life.
ex.ja: 空気と水は両方とも生命にとって欠くことができない。

ex.en: And so each citizen plays an indispensable role.
ex.ja: それで市民一人一人がなくてはならない役割をはたしている。

ex.en: He is an indispensable member for the staff.
ex.ja: そのスタッフにとって彼はなくてはならぬ存在だ。

note.ja: in（否定）+ dis（離れて）+ pens（量る）+ able。量って省くことができない →「不可欠な」。

en: A place where sick or injured people are cared for, especially a small hospital; sickhouse.
A clinic or dispensary within another institution.

infirmary.ety: From Medieval Latin infirmaria, from Latin infirmus.

ex.en: You had better go to the infirmary.
ex.ja: 君は保健室に行った方がいいぞ。

note.ja: ラテン語 infirmus（弱い）から。in（否定）+ firmus（強い）。「弱った人の所」→「診療所・保健室」。

en: To hold in or hold back; to keep in check; restrain.
To recuse.

inhibit.ety: From Latin inhibitus, perfect passive participle of inhibeō (“to hold in, check, restrain”), from in (“in, at, on”), + habeō (“to have, hold, keep”).

ex.en: Fear can inhibit learning.
ex.ja: 恐怖は学習を妨げることがある。

note.ja: in（中に）+ hib（持つ・保つ）+ it。中に押しとどめる →「抑制する・妨げる」。

To a great degree; very much.

insanely.ety:

Middle English -ly
English -ly
English insanely

ex.en: This car is insanely expensive.
ex.ja: この車はとても高い。

ex.en: It's insanely hot today.
ex.ja: 今日はばかに暑い。

ex.en: Tom is insanely rich.
ex.ja: トムはめっちゃくっちゃ金持ちなんだ。

note.ja: insane + -ly。「狂ったように」→（口語）「ものすごく」。

Among the stars.

en: Stupefied by alcohol, drunk.
Stupefied by any chemical substance.

ex.en: The ambitious man became intoxicated with his own success.
ex.ja: その野心家は自分の成功にのぼせあがった。

ex.en: The warmth after the chills intoxicated us.
ex.ja: 寒さの後の暖かさで我々はうきうきした。

ex.en: They are dancing, intoxicated with the beauty of cherry blossoms.
ex.ja: 花に浮かれて踊っている。

note.ja: intoxicate（酔わせる）+ -ed。in + toxicum（毒）。「毒が回った」→「酔った」。toxic と同じ。

Not voluntary or willing; contrary or opposed to explicit will or desire; unwilling.

note.ja: in（否定）+ voluntary（自発的な）。「無意識の・本意でない」。

Something issued.

en: Characterized by itching. (of a condition)
Feeling an itching sensation; feeling a need to be scratched. (of a person, animal or body part)

itchy.ety: From Middle English *yicchy, *ȝicchi, from Old English ġiċċiġ (“itchy”), equivalent to itch + -y. Cognate with Scots yeukie (“itchy”), West Frisian jokkerich (“itchy”), Dutch jeukachtig and jeukerig (“itchy”).

ex.en: I have athlete's foot and it's very itchy.
ex.ja: 水虫がかゆいのです。

ex.en: My head is really itchy.
ex.ja: 頭がすごくかゆいんです。

ex.en: My nose is so itchy.
ex.ja: 鼻がめちゃ痒い。

note.ja: itch（かゆみ）+ -y。「かゆい」。

en: The committee of military officers that have usurped political control.
A council, convention, tribunal or assembly; especially, the grand council of state in Spain.

junta.ety: Borrowed from Spanish junta (literally "a thing gathered or joined"), feminine form of junto, from Latin iunctus, perfect passive participle of iungō (“join”). Attested from 1623.

ex.en: The military junta took control of the country.
ex.ja: 軍事政権がその国を支配した。

note.ja: スペイン語 junta（会議・集まり）から。ラテン語 juncta（結ばれた）。「軍事政権」。junction と同じ。

en: To close or lock as if with a latch.
To catch; lay hold of.
A fastening for a door that has a bar that fits into a notch or slot, and is lifted by a lever or string from either side.
An electronic circuit that is like a flip-flop, except that it is level triggered instead of edge triggered.

latch.ety: From Middle English lacchen (“to seize, catch, grasp”, verb), from Old English læċċan (“to grasp, take hold of, catch, seize”), from Proto-Germanic *lakjaną, *lakwijaną, *lakkijaną (“to seize”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)leh₂g-, *(s)leh₂gʷ- (“to take, seize”). Cognate with Middle Dutch lakken (“to grasp, catch”).

ex.en: She lifted the latch and opened the gate.
ex.ja: 彼女は掛け金を外して門を開けた。

note.ja: 古英語 læccan（つかむ）から。「掛け金」→「しがみつく（latch onto）」。

en: A written or pictorial false statement which unjustly seeks to damage someone's reputation.
The act or tort of displaying such a statement publicly.
To defame (someone), especially in a manner that meets the legal definition of libel.
To proceed against (goods, a ship, etc.) by filing a legal claim.

libel.ety: From Middle English libel, from Old French libelle, from Latin libellus (“petition”, literally “booklet”). Doublet of libelle.

ex.en: The actress sued the magazine for libel.
ex.ja: その女優は雑誌を名誉き損で訴えた。

ex.en: Mr Miura brought an action of libel against a weekly magazine.
ex.ja: 三浦氏はある週刊誌に対して名誉毀損の訴えを起こした。

note.ja: ラテン語 libellus（小さな本）から。liber（本）。「中傷文書」→「名誉毀損」。library と同じ。

en: A band of strong tissue that connects bones to other bones.
That which binds or acts as a ligament.

ligament.ety: From Middle English ligament, from Latin ligāmentum, from ligō (“tie, bind”).

ex.en: If she's not careful she'll tear a ligament doing that.
ex.ja: もし気を付けなければ彼女はそんなことをしているうちに靭帯を切ってしまうだろう。

note.ja: ラテン語 ligamentum（ひも）から。ligare（結ぶ）。「靱帯」。league と同じ lig。

en: The state or quality of being like or alike.
Appearance or form; guise.

likeness.ety:
From Middle English liknesse, from Old English līcness, ġelīcnes (“the quality of being like or equal; likeness; image; copy; pattern; example; parable”), from Proto-West Germanic *galīkanassī (“likeness”), equivalent to like + -ness.
Cognate with West Frisian likenis (“likeness”), Dutch gelijkenis (“similarity; likeness; parable”), German Low German Glieknis (“form; semblance; likeness; parable”), German Gleichnis (“form; semblance; image; likeness; parable; simile”). The verb is derived from the noun. Compare also Old Norse líkneskja (“figure, image, appearance, likeness”).

ex.en: He bears a strong likeness to my son.
ex.ja: 彼は私の息子にとても似ている。

note.ja: like（似ている）+ -ness。「類似・肖像」。

en: High, tall, having great height or stature.
Idealistic, implying over-optimism.

lofty.ety: From Middle English lofty, lofti, lofte (“of high rank; noble; ornate”), equivalent to loft (“sky, firmament; upper room”) + -y.

ex.en: That's to me like a flower on lofty heights.
ex.ja: そんなことは私には高嶺の花です。

note.ja: loft（屋根裏・高い所）+ -y。「高くそびえる」→「高尚な」。lift と同系。

en: A utensil; tool; a weapon; (usually in compound) an article in general.
A frame or machine of wood or other material, in which a weaver forms cloth out of thread; a machine for interweaving yarn or threads int…
To appear indistinctly, e.g. when seen on the horizon or through the murk.
To appear in an exaggerated or threatening form; (of a person or thing) to tower; (of an idea) to impressively or intimidatingly occupy t…

loom.ety: From Middle English lome, from Old English *lōma, ġelōma (“tool, utensil, implement, article of furniture, household effect”) (also as andlōma, andġelōma, andlama (“utensil, instrument, implement, tool, vessel”), from Proto-West Germanic *lōmō, *lamō (“tool, utensil”), of uncertain origin. Cognate with Dutch alaam, allaam (“tool, household ware or good, appliance”), from Middle Dutch andlame. Perhaps originally meaning "a thing of frequent use, thing repeatedly needed", in which case, akin to Old English ġelōme (“often, frequently, continually, repeatedly”), from Proto-Germanic *ga- + *lōmiz,

ex.en: Dark clouds began to loom over the mountains.
ex.ja: 山の上に黒い雲が不気味に迫ってきた。

note.ja: 「ぼんやり現れる」は語源ははっきりしない。「織機」は古英語 gelōma（道具）からで別語。

en: Idiotic or unthinkable, often to the point of being funny; amusing by being plainly incongruous or absurd.

ludicrous.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin lūdicrus. First attested in 1619.

ex.en: The idea is ludicrous.
ex.ja: その考えはばかげている。

note.ja: ラテン語 ludicrus（遊びの）から。ludus（遊び）。「ばかげた」。illusion、elude と同じ lud。

en: Corn; a type of grain of the species Zea mays.

maize.ety: Borrowed from Spanish maíz, from Taíno *mahis, *mahisi, from Proto-Arawak *marikɨ. Cognate with Lokono marisi, Wayuu maiki.

ex.en: Maize is an important crop in Mexico.
ex.ja: トウモロコシはメキシコの重要な作物だ。

note.ja: スペイン語 maíz から。カリブのタイノ語 mahiz に由来する。「トウモロコシ」。

en: Intention to harm or deprive in an illegal or immoral way. Desire to take pleasure in another's misfortune.
An intention to do injury to another party, which in many jurisdictions is a distinguishing factor between the crimes of murder and mansl…
To intend to cause harm; to bear malice.

malice.ety: From Middle English malice, borrowed from Old French malice, from Latin malitia (“badness, bad quality, ill-will, spite”), from malus (“bad”).

ex.en: There was no malice in what he did.
ex.ja: 悪意でしたのではない。

ex.en: There was no malice intended in what she said.
ex.ja: 彼女のいったことには悪意は込められていなかった。

ex.en: She didn't do it out of malice.
ex.ja: 彼女は悪意からしたのではありません。

note.ja: ラテン語 malitia（悪意）から。malus（悪い）。「悪意」。malicious と同じ。

ja: 社会の周縁に追いやられた

en: Subject to marginalization.

ex.en: The program supports marginalized communities.
ex.ja: その計画は社会の周縁に追いやられた地域社会を支援している。

note.ja: marginalize（周縁に追いやる）+ -ed。margin（縁）。「社会の周縁に追いやられた」。

en: A compilation of songs assembled into a single sequence, usually encompassing many different artists and assembled by fans; often curated…
A selection of songs recorded onto a cassette tape, often combining tracks by multiple artists, whether legally obtained or informally co…

mixtape.ety:
From mix + tape; originally mix tape.
Originally referring to a homemade compilation recorded onto a cassette tape and circulated informally, especially within hip-hop culture, mixtape has broadened in sense. In contemporary usage it often denotes a musical project released outside the conventional album framework, typically characterized by looser structure, experimental material, or informal distribution, even when no physical tape medium is involved.

ex.en: He made a mixtape of his favorite songs.
ex.ja: 彼はお気に入りの曲を集めたミックステープを作った。

note.ja: mix（混ぜる）+ tape。お気に入りの曲を集めて録音したもの。

en: Materials of war: armaments, weapons and ammunition.
Bombs, rockets, missiles (complete explosive devices, in contrast to e.g. guns).
To supply with munitions.

munition.ety: From Latin mūnitiō (“a defence, fortification”) via French munition, from mūnīre (“fortify, defend (with a wall)”) + -tiō, from moenia (“city walls, defensive walls, or walls in general”). Equivalent to munite + -ion.

ex.en: The factory produced munitions during the war.
ex.ja: その工場は戦時中、軍需品を製造していた。

note.ja: ラテン語 munitio（防備）から。munire（守りを固める）。ammunition と同じ。

en: A gender-neutral title used instead of Mr (Mister), Mrs (Mistress), etc.

Mx.ety: Coined based on Mr and Ms, with x chosen as a "wildcard" character. First proposed jokingly in print in 1977.

ex.en: Mx. Tanaka, you are wanted on the phone.
ex.ja: 田中さん、電話ですよ。

ex.en: Take care of Mx. Tanaka for me, please.
ex.ja: 田中さんのことを頼むよ。

ex.en: Mx. Tanaka is a friend of ours.
ex.ja: 田中さんは私たちの友人です。

note.ja: 性別を明かさない人のための敬称。Mr. / Ms. にならって作られた。

en: An evergreen shrub or small tree of the genus Myrtus, native to southern Europe and north Africa.
A small tree or tall shrub, Cyrilla racemiflora, native to temperate and tropical regions of the Americas.

myrtle.ety: From Middle English mirtille, from Old French mirtille, mirtile, from myrte, from Latin myrtillus, from myrtus + -illus, from Ancient Greek μύρτος (múrtos, “myrtle”).

ex.en: Myrtle grows well in warm climates.
ex.ja: ギンバイカは温暖な気候でよく育つ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 myrtos から。「ギンバイカ」。

en: An enemy, especially an archenemy.
A person or character who specifically brings about the downfall of another person or character, as an agent of that character's fate or …

nemesis.ety: From the Greek goddess of retribution Nemesis (Ancient Greek Νέμεσις (Némesis)).

ex.en: The detective finally caught his old nemesis.
ex.ja: 探偵はついに長年の宿敵を捕まえた。

note.ja: ギリシャ神話の報復の女神ネメシス（Nemesis）から。nemein（分け与える）。「天罰・宿敵」。

en: The quality of being original or novel.
The capacity to think independently or be inventive.

originality.ety: From French originalité. By surface analysis, original + -ity.

ex.en: The work I'm doing now requires originality.
ex.ja: 今の仕事には、創造力が必要とされている。

ex.en: I considered his originality of great importance.
ex.ja: 私は彼の独創力がとても重要だと考えた。

ex.en: He is above all others in originality.
ex.ja: 彼は独創力では誰より勝っている。

note.ja: original（独創的な）+ -ity。「独創性」。

en: Serving as an ornament; having no purpose other than to make more beautiful.
Bred for aesthetic or decorative purposes.
An ornamental plant.

ornamental.ety:
Etymology tree
English ornament
Proto-Indo-European *h₂el-
Proto-Indo-European *-is
Proto-Indo-European *h₂élisder.?

From ornament + -al.

ex.en: The garden has many ornamental plants.
ex.ja: その庭には観賞用の植物がたくさんある。

note.ja: ornament（装飾）+ -al。「装飾用の」。

en: Belonging or relating to the pancreas.

ex.en: Pancreatic cancer is hard to detect early.
ex.ja: 膵臓がんは早期発見が難しい。

note.ja: pancreas（膵臓）+ -tic。

en: The living room of a house, or a room for entertaining guests; a room for talking; a sitting-room or drawing room.
A covered open-air patio.
Used in or appropriate for a parlor.
Advocating something in a secluded place without actual involvement or action.

parlor.ety: Inherited from Middle English parlour, from Old French parleor, parloir, parleoir, from the verb parler (“to speak”); compare Medieval Latin parlātōrium. Doublet of parloir. Displaced native Old English sprǣchūs.

ex.en: There's a beauty parlor next to the station.
ex.ja: 美容院は駅の横にあります。

ex.en: Could you suggest a good beauty parlor near here?
ex.ja: この辺によい美容院があったら教えてくれませんか。

ex.en: I'm going to open a pizza parlor.
ex.ja: ピザ屋さんを開くつもりなんだ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 parleor（話をする部屋）から。parler（話す）。「応接間」→「店」。parliament と同じ。

en: A small stone, especially one rounded by the action of water.
A particle from 4 to 64 mm in diameter, following the Wentworth scale.
To pave with pebbles.
To deposit water droplets on the ice.

pebble.ety: From Middle English pibel (also in pibleston), from Old English papolstān (“pebble-stone”), from Old English *papol, *pyppel, *pæbbel of unknown origin + Old English stān. Compare Albanian popël.

ex.en: He is not the only pebble on the beach.
ex.ja: あの男しかいないわけではないよ。

ex.en: There were eight pebbles there.
ex.ja: そこに八つの小石があった。

ex.en: She stooped to pick up a pebble.
ex.ja: 彼女は身をかがめて小石を拾い上げた。

note.ja: 古英語 papol から。「小石」。

en: Continuing in a course of action without regard to discouragement, opposition or previous failure.

perseverance.ety: From Middle English perseveraunce, from Old French perseverance, from Latin persevērantia.

ex.en: Perseverance is, among other things, necessary for success.
ex.ja: 忍耐は成功にはとりわけ必要である。

ex.en: His success came of long years of perseverance.
ex.ja: 彼の成功は長年の不屈の努力の結果だ。

ex.en: Perseverance, as you know, is the key to success.
ex.ja: 忍耐は、ご承知のように、成功への鍵です。

note.ja: persevere（やり抜く）+ -ance。per（通して）+ severus（厳しい）。「厳しさを貫くこと」→「忍耐」。

en: A health professional who controls, formulates, preserves, and dispenses medications and provides medical advice and counseling on how me…
One who studies pharmacy.

pharmacist.ety:
Etymology tree
English pharmacy
Proto-Indo-European *-id-
Proto-Indo-European *-yéti
Proto-Indo-European *-idyéti

From pharmacy (“the art of preparing drugs, a drug, especially laxatives”) + -ist.

ex.en: The pharmacist made up the prescription for me.
ex.ja: 薬剤師は処方どおりに調合してくれた。

ex.en: My grandfather was a pharmacist.
ex.ja: おじいちゃんは、薬剤師だったんだ。

note.ja: pharmacy（薬局）+ -ist。「薬剤師」。

en: Fussy; particular; demanding to have things just right.
Of food or a meal: consisting of various small items from which the diner can pick and choose.
A picture.

picky.ety:
Etymology tree
English pick
Proto-Indo-European *-kos
Proto-Germanic *-gaz
Proto-West Germanic *-g
Old English -iġ
Middle English -y
English -y
English picky
From pick + -y.

ex.en: Don't be picky about it, let's eat everything.
ex.ja: 好き嫌いせず、残さず食べましょう。

ex.en: You shouldn't be so picky about food.
ex.ja: 好き嫌い言わないで全部食べなさい。

ex.en: You shouldn't be picky about other people's work, you know?
ex.ja: 人の仕事にけちをつけるのは良くないぞ？

note.ja: pick（選ぶ）+ -y。「えり好みする」。

en: The common people of a nation.
The inhabitants of a country or one of its administrative divisions (such as a state, province, or county).

populace.ety: Borrowed from Middle French populace, from Italian popolaccio, from popolo + -accio (“pejorative suffix”), from Latin populus.

ex.en: The general populace supported the reform.
ex.ja: 一般の民衆はその改革を支持した。

note.ja: popul（人々）+ ace。人々の集まり →「大衆・民衆」。

en: Expensive, dear.

pricey.ety:
Etymology tree
English price
Proto-Indo-European *-kos
Proto-Germanic *-gaz
Proto-West Germanic *-g
Old English -iġ
Middle English -y
English -y
English pricey
From price + -y.

ex.en: These clothes are beautiful, but pricey.
ex.ja: こういう洋服はきれいだけど、値段が張るわね。

note.ja: price + -y。「値段の高い」。

en: The multiplication or natural increase in a population.
The dissemination of something to a larger area or greater number.

propagation.ety: From Middle French propagation, from Old French propagacion, from Latin propagatio. Morphologically propagate + -ion.

ex.en: The propagation of plants from cuttings is easy.
ex.ja: 挿し木で植物を増やすのは簡単だ。

note.ja: propagate（繁殖させる）+ -ion。ラテン語 propago（挿し木）。「繁殖・普及・伝播」。

en: Of, containing, generating, or reminiscent of drug-induced altered awareness, distortions of perception, hallucinations, etc.
Of graphics, etc.: having abstract shapes, bright colours, etc., reminiscent of drug-induced distortions of perception or hallucinations.
Any psychoactive substance (such as LSD or psilocybin) which, when consumed, causes perceptual changes (sometimes erratic and uncontrolla…

psychedelic.ety: From Ancient Greek ψυχή (psukhḗ, “mind, soul”) + δῆλος (dêlos, “manifest, visible”) + English -ic (prefix forming adjectives with the sense ‘of or pertaining to’), coined by the English psychiatrist Humphry Osmond (1917–2004) in a 1956 letter to Aldous Huxley.

ex.en: The album cover has psychedelic colors.
ex.ja: そのアルバムのジャケットはサイケデリックな色をしている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 psykhē（心）+ dēloun（明らかにする）。「心を開示する」→「幻覚的な」。1950年代の造語。

en: Anything which radiates or emits rays.
A device that lowers engine coolant temperature by conducting heat to the air, through metal fins.

ex.en: The radiator keeps the room warm.
ex.ja: 暖房器が部屋を暖かく保っている。

note.ja: radiate（放射する）+ -or。ラテン語 radius（光線）。「暖房器・ラジエーター」。

en: Obtained by randomization

ex.en: The study was a randomized controlled trial.
ex.ja: その研究は無作為化比較試験だった。

note.ja: randomize（無作為に並べる）+ -ed。random は古フランス語 randon（勢い）、「勢いまかせの」。

en: In the Anglican Church, a cleric in charge of a parish and who owns the tithes of it.
In the Roman Catholic Church, a cleric with managerial as well as spiritual responsibility for a church or other institution.

rector.ety: Inherited from Middle English rectour, rector, from Old French rector, rectour and Latin rēctor.

ex.en: The rector gave a speech at the graduation.
ex.ja: 学長が卒業式で式辞を述べた。

note.ja: ラテン語 rector（統治者）から。regere（治める）。regulate、correct と同じ。

en: Of, pertaining to, or suitable for royalty.
Befitting a monarch.
A small, portable organ whose sound is produced by brass beating reeds without amplifying resonators. Its tone is keen and rich in harmon…
An organ stop of the reed family, furnished with a normal beating reed, but whose resonator is a fraction of its natural length. In the 1…

regal.ety: From Middle English regal, from Old French regal (“regal, royal”), from Latin rēgālis (“royal, kingly”), from rex (“king”); also regere (“to rule”). Doublet of royal (“belonging to a monarch”), real (“unit of currency”), ariary, and riyal. Cognate with Spanish real, Italian reale, Catalan reial.

ex.en: She walked in with a regal air.
ex.ja: 彼女は堂々とした雰囲気で入ってきた。

note.ja: ラテン語 regalis（王の）から。reg（王・支配）。→「王の・堂々とした」。royal と同語源。

ja: 相対性（theory of relativity：相対性理論）

en: The state of being relative to something else; the absence of universally applicable rules or standards; relativism; (countable) an insta…
Also Einsteinian relativity: the reliance of the nature of physical phenomena (such as gravity, light, mass, and time) on the relative mo…

relativity.ety:
From relative (“connected to or depending on something else”) + -ity (suffix forming nouns from adjectives where the nouns refer to the properties, qualities, or states described by the adjectives). Sense 2.1 (“reliance of the nature of physical phenomena on the relative motion between an observer and the thing observed”) is a translation of German Relativität (“relativity”) used in the works of the German-American theoretical physicist Albert Einstein (1879–1955).
Morphologically relative + -ity.

ex.en: Few scientists understand the theory of relativity.
ex.ja: 相対性理論を理解する科学者は少ない。

ex.en: Einstein's theory of relativity is Greek to me.
ex.ja: アインシュタインの相対性理論は私にはちんぷんかんぷんだ。

ex.en: We associate Einstein with the theory of relativity.
ex.ja: アインシュタインといえば相対性理論を思い出す。

note.ja: relative（相対的な）+ -ity。re + latus（運ばれた）。「相対性」。

en: Respected or given reverence.

ex.en: He is revered as a national hero.
ex.ja: 彼は国民的英雄として崇められている。

note.ja: revere（崇める）+ -ed。ラテン語 revereri（畏れ敬う）。reverend と同じ。

en: To criticize or disapprove of someone or something through scornful jocularity; to make fun of.
Derision; mocking or humiliating words or behavior.
An object of sport or laughter; a laughing stock.

ridicule.ety:
The obsolete adjective is borrowed from French ridicule, from Latin rīdiculus (“laughable, comical, amusing, absurd, ridiculous”), from ridere (“to laugh”).
The noun is either from French, noun use of adjective, or from Latin rīdiculum, noun use of neuter of rīdiculus.
The verb is from the noun or else from French ridiculer, from ridicule.

ex.en: It is not good to ridicule him in public.
ex.ja: 公衆の面前で彼を嘲笑するのはよくない。

ex.en: It is mean of you to ridicule him in public.
ex.ja: 人前で彼を冷やかすなんて君は意地悪だ。

ex.en: If you do that, you're going to subject yourself to ridicule.
ex.ja: そんなことをすれば笑いものの種なるよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 ridiculum（笑いもの）から。ridere（笑う）。「あざける」。ridiculous と同じ。

en: A curved piece of wood attached to the bottom of a rocking chair or cradle that enables it to rock back and forth.
A rocking chair.

rocker.ety: From Middle English rokker, rockere, rokkere, equivalent to rock + -er.

ex.en: The whole world is off its rocker.
ex.ja: 世の中全体がおかしくなっているんだよ。

ex.en: Are you off your rocker?
ex.ja: バカじゃないの？

note.ja: rock + -er。「ロックをする人」と「揺れるもの（rock：揺らす）」。

en: A member of an indigenous Finno-Ugric people of Lapland.
Relating to the Sami people of northern Scandinavia, or the Sami languages.

Sami.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Sami *sāmē
Northern Sami sápmi
Northern Sami Sápmider.
English Sami
From Northern Sami Sápmi, from one of the Sami languages, of uncertain origin/meaning, but possibly related to Proto-Balto-Slavic *źémijāˀ (“land”). Displaced native Old English Finn (the direct descendant is Finn (“person from Finland”)). More at Sápmi and Sami.

ex.en: Sami drove the car at 160 miles an hour.
ex.ja: サミは時速160マイルで車を運転しました。

ex.en: Sami wants to eat some ice cream.
ex.ja: サミはアイスが食べたい。

ex.en: Sami was standing at the bus stop.
ex.ja: サミはバス停留所で立っていた。

note.ja: 北欧の先住民族の自称から。

en: A person who sculpts; an artist who produces sculpture.

sculptor.ety: Borrowed from Latin sculptor, equivalent to sculpt + -or.

ex.en: The sculptor carved wood into an image of Buddha.
ex.ja: その彫刻家は木で仏像を刻んだ。

ex.en: The sculptor belongs to the Renaissance school.
ex.ja: その彫刻家はルネサンス派に属する。

ex.en: The completion of the bronze statue did credit to the sculptor.
ex.ja: 銅像の完成はその彫刻家に名誉となった。

note.ja: ラテン語 sculpere（彫る）+ -tor。「彫刻家」。sculpture と同じ。

en: A playoff in the round with only four players or teams left, the stage before the final.
A competition that narrows a field of contestants (semifinalists) to a set of finalists, for a subsequent final.

semifinal.ety: From Latin semifinalis, equivalent to semi- + final.

ex.en: The team won the semifinals and advanced to the finals.
ex.ja: そのチームは準決勝に勝って決勝に進出した。

note.ja: semi（半分）+ final（決勝）。「準決勝」。

en: Splendor; radiance; shininess.
A thin layer of a substance (such as oil) spread on a solid or liquid surface.

sheen.ety:
From Middle English shene, schene, from Old English sċīene (“beautiful, fair, bright, brilliant, light”), from Proto-West Germanic *skaunī, from Proto-Germanic *skauniz (“beautiful”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewh₁-.
Cognate with Middle Scots schene, scheine (“beautiful, fair, attractive”), Saterland Frisian skeen (“clean, pure”), West Frisian skjin (“nice, clean”), Dutch schoon (“clean, beautiful, fair”), German schön (“beautiful”), Danish skøn (“beautiful”), Norwegian Bokmål skjønn (“beautiful”), Norwegian Nynorsk skjønn (“beautiful”), Swedish skön (“beautiful, fine”). Compare also the l

ex.en: Her hair had a healthy sheen.
ex.ja: 彼女の髪には健康的なつやがあった。

note.ja: 古英語 scēne（美しい）から。shine と同系とされる。「光沢」。

en: The quality or state of being sincere.

sincerity.ety: From Middle English sinceritie, from Old French sincerité and Medieval Latin sincēritās; both from Latin sincēritās, from sincērus + -tās. Equivalent to sincere + -ity.

ex.en: Tom is a man of absolute sincerity.
ex.ja: トムはこの上なく実直な男だ。

ex.en: You have my word on her sincerity.
ex.ja: 彼女の誠実さは私が保証します。

ex.en: I am a man of absolute sincerity.
ex.ja: 僕はこの上なく実直な男だ。

note.ja: sincere（誠実な）+ -ity。「誠実さ」。

en: Having sinned; guilty of sin.
Constituting a sin; morally or religiously wrong; wicked; evil.

sinful.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₁es-der.
Proto-Germanic *sunjō

note.ja: cheer（声援）+ leader（先導する人）。「チアリーダー」→「熱烈な支持者」。

en: A strong fortress that sits high above a city.
A stronghold or fortified place.

citadel.ety: From French citadelle, from Italian cittadella, diminutive of città (“city”), from Latin cīvitās.

ex.en: The citadel stands on a hill above the city.
ex.ja: その城砦は街を見下ろす丘の上に立っている。

note.ja: イタリア語 cittadella（小さな都市）から。città（都市）。「城砦」。city と同じ。

en: A flush-decked warship of the 17th-18th centuries having a single tier of guns; it ranked next below a frigate; called in the United Stat…
In a modern navy, a lightly armed and armoured blue water warship, smaller than a frigate, capable of transoceanic duty.

ex.en: The navy sent a corvette to patrol the coast.
ex.ja: 海軍は沿岸を巡視するためにコルベット艦を派遣した。

note.ja: フランス語 corvette から。オランダ語 korf（かご船）とされる。「コルベット艦」。

en: An upturned screen of wood or leather placed on the front of a horse-drawn carriage, sleigh or other vehicle that protected the driver fr…
A panel beneath the windshield of a vehicle or aircraft containing indicator gauges, compartments, and sometimes controls and indicator l…
To organize in a dashboard format.

dashboard.ety: From dash (“to sprinkle; to splatter”) + board for meaning 1. Possibly expanded meaning later.

ex.en: A warning light came on on the dashboard.
ex.ja: 計器盤の警告灯がついた。

note.ja: dash（泥をはね飛ばす）+ board（板）。馬車の泥よけの板 →「（車の）計器盤」→（画面の）ダッシュボード。

en: Lacking something essential; often construed with in.
Insufficient or inadequate in amount.
A person who is deficient.

deficient.ety: From Latin deficiens, present participle of deficere (“to lack, fail, be wanting”); see defect.

ex.en: The young engineer was deficient in experience.
ex.ja: その若い技師は経験が不足していた。

ex.en: The structure is deficient in harmony.
ex.ja: この建物は調和を欠いている。

ex.en: My car is deficient in horsepower.
ex.ja: 私の車は馬力が足らない。

note.ja: ラテン語 deficere（欠ける）から。de + facere。「欠けている」。deficit と同じ。

en: Having deteriorated, degraded or fallen from normal, coherent, balanced and desirable to undesirable and typically abnormal.
Having lost good or desirable qualities; hence also having bad character or habits, base, immoral, corrupt.
One who is degenerate, who has fallen from previous stature; an immoral or corrupt person.
To lose good or desirable qualities.
To cause to lose good or desirable qualities.

degenerate.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin dēgenerātus. See -ate (adjective-forming suffix) for more.

ex.en: The discussion degenerated into an argument.
ex.ja: 話し合いは口論に変わってしまった。

note.ja: de（離れて）+ genus（種族）+ -ate。「本来の性質から外れる」→「退化する・堕落した」。gene と同じ gen。

en: Pertaining to demons or evil spirits; demoniac.
Pertaining to daemons in ancient Greek thought; concerning supernatural ‘genius’.

demonic.ety: From Latin daemonicus, from Ancient Greek δαιμονικός (daimonikós, “possessed by a demon, sent by a demon”), from δαίμων (daímōn), equivalent to demon + -ic. Doublet of daimonic.

ex.en: The movie is about a demonic spirit.
ex.ja: その映画は悪魔のような霊を描いている。

note.ja: demon（悪魔）+ -ic。ギリシャ語 daimōn（神霊）。

en: Serving to deter, preventing something from happening.
Something that deters.

deterrent.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin dēterrēns, dēterrentem.

ex.en: High fines act as a deterrent to speeding.
ex.ja: 高額の罰金はスピード違反の抑止力になる。

note.ja: deter（思いとどまらせる）+ -ent。ラテン語 terrere（怖がらせる）。「抑止力」。terror と同じ。

en: A feeling of contempt or scorn.
To regard (someone or something) with strong contempt.

disdain.ety: From Middle English disdeynen, from Old French desdeignier (modern French dédaigner).

ex.en: The soldier disdained shooting an unarmed enemy.
ex.ja: その兵士は丸腰の兵士を撃つことを潔しとしなかった。

note.ja: dis（否定）+ dignari（価値があると思う）。「価値がないと思う」→「軽蔑」。dignity と同じ。

en: Bringing or warranting disgrace; shameful.
Giving offense to moral sensibilities and injurious to reputation.

ex.en: She was too proud to do anything disgraceful.
ex.ja: 彼女はプライドが高いので恥ずべきことはしなかった。

note.ja: disgrace（不名誉）+ -ful。「恥ずべき」。

en: Inspiring fear, especially in a mysterious or shadowy way; strange, weird.
Frightened, timid.
An eerie creature or thing.

eerie.ety: From Middle English eri (“fearful”), from Old English earg (“cowardly, fearful”), from Proto-West Germanic *arg, from Proto-Germanic *argaz. Akin to Scots ergh, argh from the same Old English source. Doublet of argh.

ex.en: The eerie silence struck terror into their hearts.
ex.ja: 無気味な静けさが彼らの心胆を寒からしめた。

ex.en: One image comes to mind: an eerie, pitch-black disk.
ex.ja: 頭の中に一つのイメージが湧きあがる。不気味で真っ黒な円盤。

note.ja: 古英語 earg（臆病な）から。スコットランド英語で「怖がりの」→「不気味な」。

en: Angered, made furious, made full of rage.

enraged.ety: Inherited from Middle English [Term?]. By surface analysis, enrage + -ed.

ex.en: The members of the opposition party were enraged against the bill.
ex.ja: 反対党議員はその法案に激怒した。

ex.en: Don't you know he is enraged at your insult?
ex.ja: 彼が君の侮辱を受けて怒っているのをしらないのか。

note.ja: enrage（激怒させる）+ -ed。en + rage（激怒）。

en: worn down or worn away.

ex.en: The company's competitive edge will be eroded if system engineers continue to leave.
ex.ja: ＳＥが辞め続けると会社の競争力が落ちる。

note.ja: erode（浸食する）+ -ed。e + rodere（かじる）。「かじり取られた」→「浸食された」。rodent（げっ歯類）と同じ。

en: A brief recreational trip; a journey out of the usual way.
A field trip.
To go on a recreational trip or excursion.

excursion.ety: Borrowed from Latin excursiō (“a running out, an inroad, invasion, a setting out, beginning of a speech”), from excurrere (“to run out”), from ex (“out”) + currere (“to run”). By surface analysis, excurse + -ion. Compare excursus.

ex.en: I am looking forward very much to the school excursion.
ex.ja: 私は修学旅行を大変楽しみにしている。

ex.en: Our class went on an excursion to Hakone.
ex.ja: 私たちのクラスは箱根へ遠足に行った。

ex.en: We went to Lake Towada on a school excursion.
ex.ja: 学校の遠足で十和田湖へ行った。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ curs（走る）+ ion。外へ走り出ること →「遠足・小旅行」。

en: Expressed in terms of an exponent (power of a base), the base often being 10 or e.
Characterised by a rate of change that is proportional to the value of the varying quantity, or, equivalently, by a doubling or halving o…
Any function that has an exponent as an independent variable.

ex.ja: その会社は急激な成長を遂げた。

en: A style of humor marked by broad improbabilities with little regard to regularity or method.
A motion picture or play featuring this style of humor.
To stuff with forcemeat or other food items.
To fill full; to stuff.

farce.ety: Borrowed from Middle French farce (“farce (style of humor); stuffing”) (in the latter sense, via Middle English fars, farsse), from Old French farse, from Medieval Latin farsa, from the feminine perfect passive participle of Latin farciō (“to stuff”). The theatre sense alludes to the pleasant and varied character of certain stuffed food items. Doublet of farse.

ex.en: Even before Reagan and the Supreme Court stifled it, OSHA was a farce.
ex.ja: だが、レーガン政権と最高裁判所に潰される前でさえ、ＯＳＨＡは茶番であった。

note.ja: フランス語 farce（詰め物）から。ラテン語 farcire（詰める）。劇の合間に詰め込んだ道化芝居 →「茶番・笑劇」。

en: In a deadly manner; lethally.
Ultimately, with finality or irrevocability, moving towards the demise of something.

ex.ja: その兵士は致命傷を負った。

note.ja: fatal + -ly。「致命的に」。fate と同じ。

en: An act of throwing, often violently.
An act of moving the limbs or body with violent movements, especially in a dance.
To throw with violence or quick movement; to hurl.
To move (oneself) abruptly or violently; to rush or dash.

fling.ety: From Middle English fling, from the verb (see below). Compare Icelandic flengur (“a fast sprint”).

ex.en: The enemy flung fresh troops into the battle.
ex.ja: 敵は新兵力を投入した。

ex.en: He flung a stream of abuse at me.
ex.ja: 彼は私に悪態を浴びせかけた。

ex.en: The girl flung her arms around him.
ex.ja: 少女は彼に抱きついた。

note.ja: 北欧語 flengja（むち打つ）とされる。「投げつける」→ 勢いでする「つかの間の情事」。

zh: 慌亂不安的 /慌乱不安的

en: In a state of panic, worry, frenzy, or rush.
Extremely energetic.

frantic.ety: From Middle English frantike, frentik, variant of frenetik, from Old French frenetique, from Late Latin phreneticus, alteration of phreniticus, from φρενιτικός (phrenitikós, “mad, suffering from inflammation of the brain”), from φρενῖτις (phrenîtis, “inflammation of the brain”), from φρήν (phrḗn, “the brain”). Doublet of frenetic and phrenitic.

ex.en: You did a lot of work in frantic haste.
ex.ja: あなたはたくさんの仕事を狂わんばかりに急いで片づけた。

note.ja: frenetic（狂乱の）の変化形。ギリシャ語 phrenitis（脳の炎症）。「半狂乱の・必死の」。frenzy と同じ。

en: A type of very sweet candy or confection, usually made from sugar, butter, and milk or cream.
Chocolate fudge.
To try to avoid giving a direct answer.
To alter something from its true state, as to hide a flaw or uncertainty, deliberately but not necessarily dishonestly or immorally.
Used in place of fuck.

fudge.ety: Probably a variant of fadge (“to fit”), the confectionery sense having evolved from the meaning of “merging together” or “turning out as expected”.

ex.en: Fudge! My stocking's run.
ex.ja: やだストッキング伝線しちゃってる。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。「ごまかす」→ 失敗して偶然できた菓子 →「ファッジ」。

en: To move softly, smoothly, or effortlessly.
To fly unpowered, as of an aircraft. Also relates to gliding birds and flying fish.
The act of gliding.
A transitional sound, especially a semivowel.

glide.ety:
From Middle English gliden, from Old English glīdan, from Proto-West Germanic *glīdan, from Proto-Germanic *glīdaną, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰleydʰ-.
Cognate with West Frisian glide, glydzje, Low German glieden, Dutch glijden, German gleiten, Norwegian Nynorsk gli, Danish glide, Swedish glida, Finnish liitää.

ex.en: How did you get interested in hang gliding?
ex.ja: ハンググライダーに興味を持ったきっかけは何ですか？

ex.en: Do you consider hang gliding dangerous?
ex.ja: あなたはハンググライディングが危険だと思いますか？

ex.en: The white yacht was gliding over the sea.
ex.ja: 白いヨットが海面を滑るように走っていた。

note.ja: 古英語 glīdan（滑る）から。「滑るように進む・滑空する」。glider。

en: To cause sorrow or distress to.
To feel very sad about; to mourn; to sorrow for.
A manager or steward, e.g. of a farm.

grieve.ety:
From Middle English greven, from Old French grever (“to burden”), from Latin gravō, gravāre, from adjective gravis (“grave”).
For the meaning development compare Russian тяготи́ть (tjagotítʹ, “to be a burden (on), to oppress”), Russian тужи́ть (tužítʹ, “to experience grief”), related to тяжёлый (tjažólyj, “heavy, grave”), тя́жкий (tjážkij).

ex.en: We cannot grieve over his death too deeply.
ex.ja: 彼の死は惜しんでも余りあるものだ。

ex.en: He grieved at the death of his best friend.
ex.ja: 彼は親友の死を嘆き悲しんだ。

ex.en: She has grieved over his loss for nearly ten years.
ex.ja: 彼女は十年近くも彼の死を嘆き悲しんでいる。

note.ja: ラテン語 gravare（重くする）から。griev（重い）+ e。心が重くなる →「深く悲しむ」。grief（悲しみ）。

en: Dirt, grease, soot, etc. that is ingrained and difficult to remove.
A genre of urban music that emerged in London, England, in the early 2000s, primarily a development of UK garage, dancehall, and hip hop.
To begrime; to cake with dirt.

grime.ety:
From Middle English grim (“dirt or soot covering the face”), from a specialized use of Old English grīma (“mask”), from Proto-West Germanic *grīmō, from Proto-Germanic *grīmô (“mask”).
Likely influenced by dialectal Dutch grijmsel (“grit, grime”), Dutch grijm (“soot, grime”), Middle Dutch gryme (“mask”), Middle Low German greme (“dirt”), compare Danish grime (“a halter”), Danish grimet (“soiled, stripy”), Norwegian Bokmål grimete (“soiled, stripy”), Norwegian Nynorsk grimete (“soiled, stripy”).

ex.en: It took hours to remove the grime from the oven.
ex.ja: オーブンのこびりついた汚れを落とすのに何時間もかかった。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 grime（すす）から。「こびりついた汚れ」。

en: Greatly; to a large degree, especially one large enough to be frankly appreciable.
To a serious, severe, or offensive degree.

grossly.ety:
Etymology tree
English gross
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English grossly
From gross + -ly.

ex.en: The report grossly exaggerated the problem.
ex.ja: その報告書は問題をひどく誇張していた。

note.ja: gross（ひどい・総計の）+ -ly。gross はラテン語 grossus（太い）。

en: Deep-seated and/or long-term animosity or ill will about something or someone, especially due to perceived mistreatment.
To be unwilling to give or allow (someone something).

grudge.ety:

A variant of grutch (mid 15th-century, younger than begrudge), from Middle English grucchen (“to murmur, complain, feel envy, begrudge”), from Old French grouchier, groucier (“to murmur, grumble”), of Germanic origin, probably ultimately imitative.
Akin to Middle High German grogezen (“to howl, wail”), German grocken (“to croak”). Compare also Old Norse krytja (“to murmur”), Old High German grunzen (“to grunt”).

ex.en: Tom isn't the type to hold a grudge.
ex.ja: トムは根に持つタイプではない。

ex.en: Tom is not the type to hold a grudge.
ex.ja: トムは根に持つタイプではない。

ex.en: I bear no grudge against you.
ex.ja: 君にはなんの恨みもない。

note.ja: 古フランス語 grouchier（不平を言う）から。grouch（不平家）と同じ。「恨み」。

en: The style in which someone's hair has been cut and arranged.

ex.en: The hairstyle soon became popular among young people.
ex.ja: その髪型が瞬く間に若者の間に広まった。

ex.en: The hairstyle has caught on with the girl students.
ex.ja: その髪型は女子生徒たちの間で流行した。

ex.en: She changed her hairstyle during summer vacation.
ex.ja: 彼女は夏休みの間に髪型を変えた。

note.ja: hair（髪）+ style（型）。「髪型」。

en: Written with a person's hand, as opposed to typed.

ex.en: There was a handwritten note on the door.
ex.ja: ドアには手書きのメモが貼ってあった。

ex.en: There were handwritten notes on the door.
ex.ja: ドアには手書きのメモが貼ってあった。

note.ja: hand + written。「手書きの」。

en: Pertaining to harmony.
Pleasant to hear; harmonious; melodious.
A component frequency of the signal of a wave that is an integer multiple of the fundamental frequency.
The place where, on a bowed string instrument, a note in the harmonic series of a particular string can be played without the fundamental…

harmonic.ety: From Latin harmonicus, from Ancient Greek ἁρμονικός (harmonikós), from ἁρμονία (harmonía, “harmony”). By surface analysis, harmony + -ic. Doublet of armónico.

ex.en: The singers produced a beautiful harmonic sound.
ex.ja: 歌手たちは美しく調和した音を響かせた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 harmonikos（調和の）から。「調和の・倍音の」→ harmonica。harmony と同じ。

en: A bright light, with a lens and reflector, on the front of a motor vehicle (or originally a ship or train), designed to illuminate the ro…

ex.en: The headlights don't work.
ex.ja: ヘッドライトが故障したんです。

note.ja: head（前部）+ light（明かり）。「ヘッドライト」。

en: Without feeling, emotion, or concern for others; uncaring; cruel.
Without a physical heart.

heartless.ety: From Middle English hertles, herteles, from Old English heortlēas (“without courage; listless”), equivalent to heart + -less. Cognate with German herzlos.

ex.en: It is heartless of him to say so.
ex.ja: そんなことを言うなんて彼はつれない。

ex.en: I'm not such a heartless person.
ex.ja: 俺はあんな血も涙もない人間じゃないぞ。

ex.en: He is so heartless.
ex.ja: あいつは思いやりがない。

note.ja: heart（心）+ -less。「心がない」→「無情な」。

en: Very busy with activity and confusion.

hectic.ety: From Middle English etik, ethik, from Old French etique, from Medieval Latin *hecticus, from Ancient Greek ἑκτικός (hektikós, “habitual, hectic, consumptive”), from ἕξις (héxis, “a state or habit of body or of mind, condition”), from ἔχειν (ékhein, “to have, hold, be in a certain state”).

ex.en: He leads a hectic life.
ex.ja: 彼は慌ただしい毎日を送っています。

ex.en: It's a hectic place!
ex.ja: 慌ただしい場所だな。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 hektikos（習慣的な・消耗性の）から。消耗熱の「熱っぽい」→「てんてこ舞いの」。

en: Related to holism.
Relating to a study of the whole instead of a separation into parts.

ex.en: The clinic takes a holistic approach to health.
ex.ja: その診療所は心身全体を見て健康を考えている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 holos（全体）+ -istic。「全体的な・全人的な」。catholic と同じ hol。

Of or pertaining to the menstrual cycle.

ex.ja: インフォーマントはアメリカ人２０人、イギリス人２１人という構成である。

note.ja: inform（知らせる）+ -ant。「情報提供者」。

en: To live or reside in.
To be present in.

inhabit.ety: From Old French enhabiter, from Latin inhabitāre (in + habitāre).

ex.en: Those tribes inhabit the desert all year round.
ex.ja: その部族は年中砂漠に住んでいる。

ex.en: What animals inhabit those islands?
ex.ja: その島々にはどんな動物が住んでいるのですか。

ex.en: Animals inhabit the forest.
ex.ja: 動物たちは森に住んでいる。

note.ja: in（中に）+ habitare（住む）。「住む・生息する」。habitat と同じ。

en: Tending to intrude; doing that which is not welcome; interrupting or disturbing; entering without permission or welcome.
Of rocks: forced, while in a plastic or molten state, into the cavities or between the cracks or layers of other rocks.
An igneous rock that is forced, while molten, into cracks or between other layers of rock

ex.en: The interviewer asked intrusive questions.
ex.ja: インタビュアーは立ち入った質問をした。

note.ja: intrude（侵入する）+ -sive。in + trudere（押す）。「押し入る」→「押しつけがましい」。

en: To call upon (a person, a god) for help, assistance or guidance.
To solicit, petition for, appeal to a favorable attitude.

invoke.ety: From Middle English *invoken, envoken, borrowed from Old French envoquer, from Latin invocāre (“to call upon”), itself from in- + vocare (“to call”). Doublet of invocate.

ex.en: The president invoked emergency powers.
ex.ja: 大統領は非常時の権限を発動した。

note.ja: in（〜へ）+ vok（呼ぶ）+ e。（神などに）呼びかける →「（法などを）発動する・呼び起こす」。

A foolish or stupid person.

en: Full of joy; happy.

joyous.ety: From Middle English joyous, joious, from Old French joieus, from joie + -eus.

ex.en: May happiness and joy come to you as you celebrate this joyous day.
ex.ja: この喜ばしい日をお祝いし、幸せと喜びがあなたにきますように。

note.ja: joy + -ous。「喜ばしい」。

A New Zealand dollar.

A small plant leaf.
To distribute leaflets to.
To distribute leaflets.

en: The time or hour at or around which lunch is normally eaten.
A break in work or school to eat lunch.

ex.en: We should get to Chicago by lunchtime.
ex.ja: 私たちはお昼までにシカゴに着かなければならない。

ex.en: She's supposed to be back by lunchtime.
ex.ja: 彼女は昼食の時間までには帰ってくることになってます。

ex.en: We pigged out on pizza and chicken at lunchtime.
ex.ja: 僕たちは昼飯にピザとチキンをたらふく食べた。

note.ja: lunch（昼食）+ time（時間）。「昼食時」。

en: In the International System of Units, the derived unit of illuminance or illumination; one lumen per square metre. Symbol: lx

lux.ety: Borrowed from Latin lūx (“light”), from Proto-Indo-European *lewk- (“white; light; bright”). Cognates include Ancient Greek λευκός (leukós, “white, blank, light, bright, clear”), Ancient Greek λύκη (lúkē, “light, morning twilight”), Sanskrit रोचते (rocate), Middle Persian 𐭩𐭥𐭬 (rōz, “day”) and Old English lēoht (noun) (English light).

ex.en: The room's lighting is about 500 lux.
ex.ja: その部屋の照度は約５００ルクスだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 lux（光）から。照度の単位。lucid、illuminate と同系。

en: A heavy fighting club.
A ceremonial form of this weapon.
To hit someone or something with a mace.

mace.ety: From Middle English mace, borrowed from Old French mace, mache, from Vulgar Latin *mattia, *mattea, matia, (compare Italian mazza, Spanish maza), probably from Proto-West Germanic *mattjō (“cutting tool, hoe”).

ex.en: The guard carried a heavy mace.
ex.ja: 衛兵は重い矛を持っていた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 mace（こん棒）から。「矛」→ 権威の象徴 →（議会の）職杖。香辛料のメースは別語。

en: Harmful, malevolent, injurious.
Tending to produce death; threatening a fatal issue.
A deviant; a person who is hostile or destructive to society.

malignant.ety: From Middle French malignant, from Late Latin malignans. See malign.

ex.en: The tumor is malignant.
ex.ja: 腫瘍は悪性です。

note.ja: ラテン語 malignare（悪意をもって行う）から。malus（悪い）+ gignere（生む）。「悪性の」。benign（良性の）と対。

zh: 獅子的鬃毛 /狮子的鬃毛

en: Longer hair growth on back of neck of an animal, especially a horse or lion.
Long or thick hair of a person's head.

mane.ety:
From Middle English mane, mayne, from Old English manu (“mane”), from Proto-West Germanic *manu, from Proto-Germanic *manō (“mane”), from Proto-Indo-European *mony-, *mon- (“neck”).
Cognate with Dutch maan, manen (“mane”), German Mähne (“mane”), Danish man (“horse's mane”), Swedish man (“horse's mane”), Icelandic mön (“mane”).

ex.en: The lion shook its golden mane.
ex.ja: ライオンは金色のたてがみを揺らした。

note.ja: 古英語 manu（たてがみ）から。「たてがみ」。

en: A cosmetic used to darken and thicken the eyelashes.
To apply mascara to the eyelashes

ex.en: She put on some mascara before going out.
ex.ja: 彼女は出かける前にマスカラを塗った。

note.ja: スペイン語 máscara（仮面）から。mask と同じ語源。

A service aiming to bring together sellers and buyers or potential partners.

en: Unbranded.
Showing independence in thoughts or actions.
An unbranded range animal.
Anything dishonestly obtained.
To take an unbranded range animal.
To seize without a legal claim.

maverick.ety:
Named after Texan lawyer and politician Samuel Maverick (1803–1870), who refused to brand his cattle. For probable origin and meaning, see Maverick.
The poker noun sense (“a queen and a jack as a starting hand in Texas hold ’em”) may be from the theme song of the US Western television series Maverick (1957–1962), which says of the eponymous protagonist that “[g]amblin’ is his game” and that he is “livin’ on jacks and queens”.

ex.en: He is a maverick in the world of politics.
ex.ja: 彼は政界の一匹狼だ。

note.ja: 19世紀テキサスの牧場主マーベリック（Maverick）から。自分の牛に焼き印を押さなかったことから。

en: An acute and highly contagious disease which often afflicts children caused by the virus Measles morbillivirus and causing red rashes, fe…
Synonym of cysticercosis: A disease of livestock or meat caused by the presence of tapeworm larvae.

measles.ety: Either from Middle Dutch masels (“blood blisters, measels”) or Middle Low German maselen (“red blemishes, measels”), both from Old High German masala (“blood blister, phlegmon”). Doublet of measlings. Cognate with mazer & mase and Middle Low German masele & māsel. Influenced in pronunciation and some senses by mesel (“leprous, leper”).

ex.en: He had three-day measles the other day.
ex.ja: 先日三日ばしかにかかりました。

ex.en: Love is like measles - everyone should experience it.
ex.ja: 恋愛は、はしかのようなものだ。みんな一度はかからなければならない。

ex.en: Measles can be quite dangerous.
ex.ja: はしかにかかると非常に危険なこともある。

note.ja: 中英語 maseles（斑点）から。中世オランダ語 masel（しみ）。「はしか」。

en: To physically repair (something that is broken, defaced, decayed, torn, or otherwise damaged).
To add fuel to (a fire).
An act of repairing.
A place in a thing (such as a tear in clothing) which has been repaired.

ex.en: How soon can I have my shoes mended?
ex.ja: 靴はいつまでに直してもらえますか。

ex.en: I had my shoes mended at that store.
ex.ja: 私は靴をあの店で直してもらった。

ex.en: He got his wife to mend his shirt.
ex.ja: 彼は奥さんにシャツを縫ってもらった。

note.ja: amend（改める）の短縮。「修理する・繕う」。

Small; tiny; minuscule.
A microbe or bacterium.

en: A severe, disabling headache, usually affecting only one side of the head, and often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, photophobia and vis…
A neurological condition characterised by such headaches.

migraine.ety: First appears c. 1425. A respelling (following French) of the late 14th century Middle English megrim, from the 13th century Old French migraigne, from Vulgar Latin pronunciation of Latin hemicrania (“a pain in one half of the head”), from Ancient Greek ἡμικρανία (hēmikranía), from ἡμι- (hēmi-, “hemi-, half”) + κρανίον (kraníon, “the skull”) (whence also cranium), a calque of Egyptian gs-tp (“a headache”), from gs (“half”) + tp (“the head”), although the link between the Egyptian magical papyri and the Greek ἡμικρανία (hēmikranía) could be purely incidental. Cognate to megrim, hemicrania.

ex.en: I have a migraine.
ex.ja: 偏頭痛がします。

ex.en: For years, Tom suffered from migraine headaches.
ex.ja: トムは何年も偏頭痛に苦しんだ。

ex.en: Tom suffered from migraine headaches for years.
ex.ja: トムは何年も偏頭痛に苦しんだ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 hēmikrania（頭の半分）から。hēmi（半分）+ kranion（頭蓋）。片側の頭が痛むことから。cranium と同じ。

en: A mitten
An oversized, protective glove such as an oven mitt or a baseball mitt.

ex.en: The catcher caught the ball in his mitt.
ex.ja: 捕手はミットでボールを受けた。

note.ja: mitten（ミトン）の短縮。「（野球の）ミット」。

en: Any of a number of winds associated with regions where most rain falls during a particular season.
Tropical rainy season when the rain lasts for several months with few interruptions.

monsoon.ety: Borrowed from Portuguese monção and Dutch moesson, from Arabic مَوْسِم (mawsim, “season”), from وَسَمَ (wasama, “to mark, to brand”).

ex.en: The monsoon brings heavy rain every summer.
ex.ja: 季節風が毎年夏に大雨をもたらす。

note.ja: アラビア語 mawsim（季節）からポルトガル語・オランダ語を経た語。「季節風・雨季」。

en: A composite work, particularly an artwork, created by assembling or putting together other elements such as pieces of music, pictures, te…
The art or process of doing this.
To combine into, or depict as, a montage.

ex.en: The film opens with a montage of old photos.
ex.ja: その映画は古い写真のモンタージュで始まる。

note.ja: フランス語 monter（組み立てる）から。「モンタージュ」。mount と同じ。

en: Careless or inattentive.
Culpable due to negligence.

negligent.ety: From Middle English necligent, negligent, from Old French negligent, from Latin negligēns.

ex.en: You are too negligent of those around you.
ex.ja: 君は周囲の人に無関心すぎるよ。

ex.en: She is very negligent in her dress.
ex.ja: 彼女は身なりをかまわない。

ex.en: He was negligent of his duties.
ex.ja: 彼は職務怠慢だった。

note.ja: ラテン語 neglegere（怠る）から。neg + legere（拾う）。「怠慢な」。neglect と同じ。

en: Nothing; zero.
A score of zero
No, not any.

nil.ety:
Borrowed from Latin nīl, a contraction of nihil, nihilum (“nothing”). See
nihilism, nihility.

ex.en: The chance of winning is almost nil.
ex.ja: 勝てる見込みはほとんどゼロだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 nihil（無）の短縮。「無・ゼロ」。annihilate（全滅させる）と同じ。

en: Any of the natural substances, such as an endorphin, released in the body in response to pain; an endogenous opioid.
Any of a group of synthetic compounds that exhibit similarities to the opium alkaloids that occur in nature.

opioid.ety: Attested 1963; from opium + -oid, to distinguish from opiate.

ex.en: The country is facing an opioid crisis.
ex.ja: その国はオピオイド問題に直面している。

note.ja: opium（アヘン）+ -oid（〜のようなもの）。ギリシャ語 opion（ケシの汁）。

ex.ja: 美咲は新しく出会った人と熱烈な恋をしました。

en: An agent that can cause disease, especially an infectious microorganism, such as a bacterium, virus, protozoon or fungus.

pathogen.ety: From patho- + -gen. Second element ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁- (“lineage”) through Ancient Greek γένος (génos, “birth”)

ex.en: The pathogen spreads through water.
ex.ja: その病原体は水を介して広がる。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 pathos（病気・苦しみ）+ -gen（生み出すもの）。「病原体」。pathology と同じ。

en: The act of persuading, or trying to do so; the addressing of arguments to someone with the intention of changing their mind or convincing…
An argument or other statement intended to influence one's opinions or beliefs; a way of persuading someone.

persuasion.ety: From French persuasion and its source, Latin persuāsiō, from persuādēre, from suādēre (“to advise, recommend”).

ex.en: Finally, he gave in to my persuasion.
ex.ja: ついに、彼は私の説得に成功した。

ex.en: Finally, he gave into my persuasion.
ex.ja: ついに、彼は私の説得くっした。

ex.en: Crude persuasion is to persistently egg someone on.
ex.ja: 幼稚な説得とは、人をしつこく唆すことだ。

note.ja: persuade（説得する）+ -sion。per + suadere（勧める）。「説得・信条」。

en: The replaying of something previously recorded, especially sound or moving images.

playback.ety: From play + back. Sense 2 is from French playback, a pseudo-anglicism of this term.

ex.en: Press the button to start playback.
ex.ja: ボタンを押すと再生が始まります。

note.ja: play back（再生する）の名詞化。「再生」。

en: Very extravagant.
Very expensive, or appearing expensive; opulent, luxurious.
A textile fabric with a nap or shag on one side, longer and softer than the nap of velvet.
A plush toy.
To give a soft, fluffy surface to.

plush.ety: From French peluche (“fluff, plush”). The fact that historically (in past centuries) plush upholstery was so expensive as to be socially exclusive undoubtedly connects the senses of "luxurious" and "soft".

ex.en: The hotel lobby has plush sofas.
ex.ja: そのホテルのロビーには豪華なソファがある。

Precedent.

precedence.ety: From Middle French précédence (“the state of preceding, anteriority”). Morphologically precede + -ence.

en: Unspoiled; still with its original purity; uncorrupted or unsullied.
Primitive, pertaining to the earliest state of something.

pristine.ety: From Middle French pristin, borrowed from Latin prīstinus.

ex.en: The beach was pristine and quiet.
ex.ja: その浜辺は手つかずで静かだった。

note.ja: ラテン語 pristinus（昔の・原初の）から。「元のままの・まっさらな」。prime と同系。

ex.ja: ジェット機はプロペラ機よりもずっと速い。

en: An implement with a handle connected to a round frame strung with wire, sinew, or plastic cords, and used to hit a ball, such as in tenni…
A snowshoe formed of cords stretched across a long and narrow frame of light wood.
To strike with, or as if with, a racket.

racket.ety:
From Middle English raket, of uncertain origin.
Possibly cognate with Middle French rachette, requette (“palm of the hand”). From Arabic رَاحَةْ اَلْيَد (rāḥat al-yad, “palm of the hand”).
Alternatively, the term might be derived from Dutch raketsen instead, from Middle French rachasser (“to strike (the ball) back”).

ex.en: You have the same racket as I have.
ex.ja: 君は僕と同じラケットを持っている。

ex.en: Send me a racket and my tennis shoes.
ex.ja: ラケット１本とテニスシューズを送ってください。

ex.en: It was this racket that Mike bought yesterday.
ex.ja: マイクが昨日買ったのはこのラケットでした。

note.ja: 「ラケット」はアラビア語 rāḥa（手のひら）からフランス語を経た語。「騒音・不正な商売」は擬音的な別語。

The operation of accessing data, either from memory or from a storage device.

note.ja: retrieve（取り戻す）+ -al。「回収・検索」。

en: Indirect, circuitous, or circumlocutionary.
Encircling; enveloping; comprehensive.
A road junction at which traffic streams circularly around a central island.
A horizontal wheel which rotates around a central axis when pushed and on which children ride, often found in parks as a children's play …
To play on a roundabout (carousel)
To travel round roundabouts

ex.ja: 回りくどい言い方はしないでくれ。

ex.en: What I want to ask is how roundabout should I be?
ex.ja: 私がお聞きしたいのは、どのくらい言葉をオブラートに包めばいいのかということです。

ex.en: I think I will take a roundabout way to return home.
ex.ja: 今日は遠回りをして帰ろっと。

note.ja: round（回って）+ about（周りを）。「回り道の」→「遠回しの」、（英）「環状交差点」。

en: Containing salt; salty.
Resembling salt.
Water containing dissolved salt.
A salt spring; a place where salt water is collected in the earth.

 *sḗh₂l
From Middle English salyne, from Medieval Latin salīna and Middle French salin, from Latin sal (“salt”).

ex.en: Show me how to make 10% saline solution.
ex.ja: 濃度10%の食塩水の作り方を教えてください。

ex.ja: あのさ恭平、この問題・・・食塩水のやつなんだけど・・・。

en: UK and Canada spelling of savior.

ex.en: Jesus Christ is my saviour.
ex.ja: イエス･キリストは私の救い主です。

note.ja: savior のイギリスのつづり。ラテン語 salvator。save と同じ。

en: Probably not.
Certainly not, hardly at all.

scarcely.ety: From Middle English scarcely, scarsly, scarsely, scarsliche, scarseliche, equivalent to scarce + -ly.

ex.en: There are scarcely any flowers in our garden.
ex.ja: 家の庭に花はほとんど見られません。

ex.en: Mary scarcely seems to care for me, does she?
ex.ja: メアリーは私が好きではないみたいですね。

ex.en: What he said can scarcely be true.
ex.ja: 彼の言ったことはまさか本当であるとは思えない。

note.ja: scarce（乏しい）+ -ly。ラテン語 excerpere（摘み取る）。「ほとんど〜ない」。

en: The construction of ships.
A construction of a ship.

ex.en: The town was once famous for shipbuilding.
ex.ja: その町はかつて造船で有名だった。

note.ja: ship（船）+ building（建造）。「造船」。

en: A lifting of the shoulders to signal indifference or a casual lack of knowledge about something.
A cropped, cardiganlike garment with short or long sleeves, typically knitted.
To raise (the shoulders) to express uncertainty, lack of concern, (formerly) dread, etc.

shrug.ety: From Middle English schruggen, shrukken, probably of North Germanic origin related to Danish skrugge, skrukke (“to stoop; crouch”), Swedish skruga, skrukka (“to huddle; crouch”), all from or related to Old Norse skrykkva, from Proto-Germanic *skrinkwaną. Compare also Old English scrincan (“to shrink”). More at shrink.

ex.en: The U.S. economy shrugged off the '87 Crash.
ex.ja: アメリカ経済は１９８７年の大暴落からいち早く回復していますね。

ex.en: She gave a shrug of the shoulders.
ex.ja: 彼女は肩をすくめた。

ex.en: He simply shrugged off my suggestion.
ex.ja: 彼は私の示唆に単に肩をすくめて無視した。

note.ja: 中英語 schruggen（身を縮める）から。「肩をすくめる」。

en: Filled with smoke.
Filled with or enveloped in tobacco smoke.

smoky.ety: From Middle English smoke, smokei, smoki, smokie, smoky, equivalent to smoke + -y (adjectival suffix). Doublet of Samoki.

ex.en: The atmosphere in the room was hot and smoky.
ex.ja: その部屋の空気は暑く煙が立ち込めていた。

ex.en: It's very smoky in here.
ex.ja: ここん中、めちゃ煙たいな。

ex.en: It's too smoky here.
ex.ja: ここは煙たすぎる。

note.ja: smoke（煙）+ -y。「煙たい」。

en: A garden tool with a handle and a flat blade for digging. Not to be confused with a shovel which is used for moving earth or other materi…

To turn over soil with a spade to loosen the ground for planting.
To move with a spade, or as with a spade.

spade.ety: From Middle English spade, from Old English spada, spade, spadu (“spade”), from Proto-Germanic *spadô. Doublet of spatha, spathe, and épée.

ex.en: Spades are the trump suit.
ex.ja: スペードはトランプのマークです。

ex.en: Jane calls a spade a spade.
ex.ja: ジェーンは、白黒をはっきりさせる人です。

ex.en: Call a spade a spade.
ex.ja: 鋤は鋤と呼べ。

note.ja: 古英語 spadu（鋤）から。トランプのスペードはスペイン語 espada（剣）からで別語。

en: Moderate; not excessive.
Specifically, moderate in temperature.

temperate.ety: The adjective is first attested in 1380, in Middle English, the verb in 1540; borrowed from Latin temperātus, perfect passive participle of temperō (“to moderate, forbear, combine properly”), see -ate (adjective-forming suffix) and -ate (verb-forming suffix). See temper. Displaced native Old English ġemetegod.

ex.en: Our country's climate is temperate.
ex.ja: 我々のところの気候は温帯性です。

ex.en: They can be found around the world in temperate and tropical oceans.
ex.ja: それらは、世界中の温帯、熱帯の海洋で見られます。

note.ja: ラテン語 temperare（ほどよく混ぜる）から。ほどよい →「温暖な・節度ある」。temper、temperature も同じ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 treble から。ラテン語 triplus（3倍の）。triple と同じ語源。

en: A sky-blue, greenish-blue, or greenish-gray semi-precious gemstone.
A pale greenish-blue colour, like that of the gemstone.
Made of turquoise (the gemstone).
Having a pale greenish-blue colour.

turquoise.ety:
From Middle French turquoise, from Old French (pierre) turquoise (“Turkish (stone)”), from turc + -ois. The stone, mined near Nishapur in the Khorasan region of Persia, was originally brought to Europe through Turkey. Doublet of Turkish.
Compare typologically copper (<< Ancient Greek Κύπρος (Kúpros, “Cyprus”)).

ex.en: She wore a turquoise necklace.
ex.ja: 彼女はトルコ石のネックレスをしていた。

note.ja: フランス語 turquoise（トルコの（石））から。トルコ経由でヨーロッパに入ったことから。
